# poolinfo <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/joonho112/poolinfo/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/joonho112/poolinfo/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
<!-- badges: end -->

A multisite trial, a meta-analysis or a small area estimation problem gives
an estimate and a standard error for each site. A hierarchical model shrinks
each estimate toward the overall mean, and the weight that a site's
posterior mean keeps on its own estimate is the site's reliability.
poolinfo summarizes the reliabilities of all the sites at once: their
informativeness (the reliability at the geometric mean of the sampling
variances), their mean, their dispersion, and a count of how the total
reliability is shared among the sites. It computes the posterior
distribution of each from the estimates and their standard errors, and it
plots them. The summaries are worth checking before you rank sites, report
site effects or study how an effect varies across sites, because they measure
how much of each site's own estimate survives the pooling. The diagnostics
are those of Lee (2026).

## Installation

You can install poolinfo from GitHub with:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("joonho112/poolinfo", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The vignettes are also on the
[package website](https://joonho112.github.io/poolinfo/).

## Example

The data set `ocrs` has the estimated effects of an online credit recovery
course on course passing in the 32 school-by-subject sites of the Online
Credit Recovery Study ([Rickles et al.,
2024](https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2023.2198524)), with their standard
errors. `reliability_posterior()` computes the posterior distribution of the
diagnostics by numerical integration over the between-site standard
deviation, with a flat prior on it and on the mean.

```{r fit}
library(poolinfo)
fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, site = site, data = ocrs,
                             scale_label = "risk difference")
fit
```

```{r facts, include = FALSE}
ps <- profile_summary(fit)
val <- function(q, col = "mean") ps[[col]][ps$quantity == q]
num <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
pct <- function(x) round(100 * x)
stopifnot(val("I", "lower") < 0.5, prob_above(fit) > 0.95, val("J_eff") > 31)
```

The informativeness is `r num(val("I"))`, with a 95% posterior interval from
`r num(val("I", "lower"))` to `r num(val("I", "upper"))`, so a site whose
sampling variance is the geometric mean of the 32 keeps about
`r pct(val("I"))`% of its own estimate in its posterior mean. The mean
reliability, `r num(val("mean"))`, is close to it, the dispersion is
H = `r num(val("H"), 3)`, and the concentration count is
`r num(val("J_eff"), 1)` of 32, so the total reliability is shared almost
evenly among the sites. Every summary is conditional on the standard
errors, which the model treats as known.

`plot()` shows the site estimates and their posterior means, the sorted
reliabilities, the posterior density of the informativeness and the plane
of the informativeness and the logit variance.

```{r dashboard, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 9, fig.alt = "Four panels: the site estimates and their posterior means with intervals; the sorted site reliabilities with the informativeness and its band; the posterior density of the informativeness; and the informativeness and logit variance plane."}
plot(fit, scale = 100)
```

## What else is in the package

- Diagnostics of a profile at a fixed between-site standard deviation:
  `reliability_profile()`, `kl_centroid()`, `kl_dispersion()`,
  `concentration_count()` and related functions.
- Diagnostics from fits of other packages: `reliability_draws()` for
  posterior draws (from brms, for example), and methods for metafor, ebnm
  and multisiteDGP objects; `map_tau2_interval()` maps a confidence interval
  for the between-site variance.
- Planning: `reliability_design()`, `balanced_allocation()` and
  `solve_design()` give the profile of a planned trial and allocations of
  a total or a budget to the sites.
- Comparing and reporting: `compare_profiles()`, `prior_sensitivity()`,
  `report_table()` and `report_text()`.

`vignette("poolinfo")` walks through the example above in full.

## Citation

To cite poolinfo, use `citation("poolinfo")`. The diagnostics are those of

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid
diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.
